opening.argument: The panel is devoted to self-custody trends and wallet usability, with speakers examining how cryptocurrency interfaces can become easier to use. One speaker identifies “which is user interface and experience, with a lot of wallets,” while another describes human language as “the ultimate interface for interfacing with crypto.” The discussion also treats custody choices and privacy concerns, including whether people should give up ownership to custodial services and whether users should present personal information merely to use a wallet. References to fake IDs, scammers, and USDT transfers serve to explain KYC responsibilities and platform risks: “KYC at the end of the day is a necessary evil,” and platforms should not allow “bad people to use your platform.” Taken together, these are educational and operational discussions about self-custody, wallet design, and regulation, not an offer or request to move funds or disclose data.
